title: Billie Holiday's birth chart
metaDescription: Billie Holiday's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 16.8° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the nine placements whose signs are settled stand in Pisces — Mercury, Venus, Mars and Jupiter. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 16.8° into Aries — the second decan, which the old scheme hands to the Sun. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Mercury holds 25.0° Pisces, Venus holds 7.1° Pisces, Mars holds 22.9° Pisces — in the old shorthand, thought steeped in tone and memory; attraction that works by atmosphere; effort that surges when it matters.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mercury and Saturn hold the closest angle here — a square, 1.9° wide. The old texts treat a square as the aspect you feel earliest and thank latest: obstruction first, competence afterwards. Behind it, the Sun sextile Uranus at 1.9°, and Mercury conjunction Mars at 2.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Venus makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks four placements here. The Sun in Aries at 16.8° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mercury in Pisces at 25.0° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Pisces at 7.1° is in exaltation; Jupiter in Pisces at 14.8° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 6 water, 2 air, 1 fire; by modality, 5 mutable, 3 cardinal, 1 fixed. No settled placement falls in earth — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Neptune was retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Capricorn into Aquarius during that day at the birthplace, travelling 13.5° between one midnight and the next. The hour would decide it; no hour was recorded. The reading keeps the question open rather than flipping a coin dressed as astrology.
